newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank lowers overnight rates.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank lowers overnight rates.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Tuesday it cut its overnight borrowing rate to 10.75 from 11.0 percent.
It lowered its overnight lending rate to 13.25 from 14.0 percent.
The Central Bank did not give any reason for the cut in overnight rates at the money market.
But a trader said "it's a reflection of the liquidity in the market. It's so flooded with money."
Traders said some 4.9 billion pesos in Treasury notes and 5.1 billion pesos in Treasury bills are expected to mature this week.

The money returning into the system had limited alternative outlets since the Bureau of Treasury did not hold its regular weekly 3.5 billion-peso Treasury bill auction this week in view of the holidays for the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, traders said.
Since Friday, the Central Bank kept its reverse repos and special series T-bills closed, they said.
Traders believe the Central Bank's actions may have been prompted by the encouraging money supply growth indicators.
The Central Bank reported on Monday base money in November slackened to a year-on-year growth of 7.6 percent from 13.2 percent in the previous month.
Year-on-year growth of reserve money, a main determinant of base money, also decelerated to 8.4 percent in November from 13.7 the previous month.
